segments.t: Determined to make back the money Kostya just lost on the broken bottles, Nastya approaches Dmitry Nagiyev and pitches her husband as the restaurant's new wine steward.
Кажется, я нашла нам нового сомелье.
Он не пьёт и не курит.
Красивый и очень хороший семьянин.
Это наш бармен Костя.
Ты своего мужа мне предлагаешь?
Он сегодня три бутылки разбил!
Но ведь за свой счёт!
Вы же добрый и щедрый человек.
И лучший ведущий всей страны!
Ладно, к вечеру будь готов.
Я устрою тебе дегустацию вин.
Настя, я же не разбираюсь в винах!
Главное — вовремя сказать прекрасный выбор.
Твоя жена и ребёнок уверены, что получится.
Let's walk through Nastya's bold pitch and Kostya's panic.
Кажется, я нашла нам нового сомелье.
'It seems I have found us a new sommelier.' Nastya frames one memorable word for Kostya: "kazhetsya" means "it seems, I think" (from "kazatsya"), giving the line its exact edge.
Он не пьёт и не курит.
'He does not drink and does not smoke.' Nastya pushes back frankly with a smile, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
Красивый и очень хороший семьянин.
'Handsome and a very good family man.' Nastya jumps in pointedly toward Kostya, testing Kostya's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
Это наш бармен Костя.
'It is our bartender Kostya.' Nastya points to this vivid choice right here: "barmen" means "bartender", and it carries the main weight of what Nastya is saying.
Ты своего мужа мне предлагаешь?

'Are you pitching your own husband to me?' Nagiyev offers that point to Kostya: Russian keeps the exact word order of a normal statement here, turning it into a question for Kostya purely through rising pitch at the end.
Он сегодня три бутылки разбил!
'He smashed three bottles today!' Nagiyev follows up lightly in this moment, making his position completely clear.
Но ведь за свой счёт!
'But at his own expense, after all!' Nastya chooses one concrete element toward Kostya: "schyot" means "counting, account", and it carries the main weight of what Nastya is saying.
Вы же добрый и щедрый человек.

'You are a kind and generous person, after all.' Nastya states this answer plainly here: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
И лучший ведущий всей страны!
'And the best TV host in the whole country!' Nastya follows up frankly during the talk, making her position completely clear.
Ладно, к вечеру будь готов.
'Fine, be ready by evening.' Nagiyev reaches for one direct touch for Nastya: "vecheru" means "evening" (from "vecher"), giving the line its exact edge.
Я устрою тебе дегустацию вин.
'I will set up a wine tasting for you.' Nagiyev picks one classic piece right here: "degustatsiyu" means "tasting" (from "degustatsiya"), giving the line its exact edge.
Настя, я же не разбираюсь в винах!
'Nastya, I do not know anything about wines!' Kostya chimes in openly with a smile, bringing things back to earth after the buildup.
Главное — вовремя сказать прекрасный выбор.
'The main thing is to say 'excellent choice' Nastya reaches for one concrete element with Kostya: "prekrasnyy" means "beautiful", and it carries the main weight of what Nastya is saying.
Твоя жена и ребёнок уверены, что получится.

'Your wife and child are sure that you will succeed.' Nastya shapes this point in earnest: the "-sya" ending on "poluchitsya" ("will come out") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.

That wraps up this scene as determined to save their family budget, Nastya flatters Nagiyev into giving Kostya a trial as the new sommelier that evening, despite Kostya's total ignorance of wine. Until next time!
